title: Mac TermAl binary code-signing identity for keychain ACL continuity across builds
outcome: macOS keychain ACLs for an unsigned or ad-hoc-signed binary re-prompt when the binary changes. So every Mac TermAl install may need Greg's "Always Allow", or fail with -25308 (errSecInteractionNotAllowed) under launchd when TermAl reads its TermAl.Federation credentials. The durable fix is a stable code-signing identity for the Mac TermAl binary, so the keychain item's designated requirement survives rebuilds. Greg creates the identity, the private-key act being his. This child applies the signing at install, so an installed build reads the credential without interaction. Raised by Architect1 in note a12cfdc5 on w-dc87205501a1 (§E). The read-only credential probe there, on the S3 build, discriminates whether this bites before the run-as-greg cutover.
acceptance: Evidence on the S3 or a later build shows whether the installed Mac TermAl binary, running as the host's user in its launch context, reads the existing TermAl.Federation item without interaction after a rebuild (OS status recorded, never the value).

If it does not, a code-signing identity created by Greg is applied at install so that two successive installs both read the item without a prompt, with the signing step recorded in the Mac install instruction.
